notes: Ethiopia's Master Facility Registry (MFR) publishes no API documentation and no machine spec — the Swagger UI its adaptor README points at (https://mfr.moh.gov.et/swagger/index.html) is gone, and every well-known spec path on the API host 404s — so this spec was built by observing the live production API directly, which answers anonymously on its read endpoints. That is why it is best-effort: routes not reachable anonymously cannot be proven absent. Method sets were enumerated from the Allow header ASP.NET returns on a 405, request models from the type names in its 400 validation problems, and field types were aggregated over 600 real facility records; a handful of always-null columns (numberOfNurse and its siblings, otherDiagnosticAndImagingServices) are typed from their named siblings rather than from an observed value. This replaces a five-endpoint hand-authored subset that used the wrong host and omitted the /api prefix: 14 operations across facilities, the region/zone/woreda hierarchy, the shared reference-data lookups and the health probe, with 30 schemas. Four endpoints exist but are protected by the Ministry of Health SSO (POST/PUT /api/Facility, DELETE /api/Facility/{dhis2Id}, POST /api/Lookup) — they are documented with their route and auth confirmed, and their request bodies left as free-form objects rather than invented, since they could not be exercised. Every call answers the envelope { result, message, model }, and note that `result` is the API's own status (0 ok, 1 rejected) which is independent of the HTTP status: an unknown lookup name still answers 200. Because `model` is not one of the envelope keys data-objects recognises, data-schemas/index.json lists the envelope schemas as the resources and the domain objects (Facility, Region, Zone, Woreda, LookupItem, FacilitySummary) come along in the closure instead — the adaptor itself unwraps `model` onto state.data. Cross-reference against the adaptor: get/post/request are generic, and every path its JSDoc and tests exercise (Location/Regions, Facility?id=, Facility/All, Facility/GetFacilities, Facility/ExportCSV) is present with the method the live API actually accepts — note that GetFacilities and ExportCSV are POST-only upstream (a GET on either falls through to the GET /api/Facility/{dhis2Id} route and 404s), and that the CSV export is served as application/csv, which the adaptor reads with parseAs: 'text'. The mock sandbox diverges from the live API in three ways that belong to the mocker, not to this spec: it serves GetFacilities/ExportCSV over GET, it returns bare arrays and objects instead of the { result, message, model } envelope, and it answers 201 with a bare body on POST /api/Facility.
